record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Study examples of "quadratic + linear" Poisson pencils. Compute their algebraic types and construct complete families of polynomials in bi-invol ution for such pencils. It is a very general question whether or not a given symplectic (Pois son) manifold M admits an integrable system with good properties. In particular, if M is a vector space endowed with a polynomial Poisson bracket, we are interested in integrable systems defined o n M by a collection of Poisson commuting polynomials. For a linear Poisson bracket (5.3), such a poly nomial integrable system always exists. This statement, known as Mischenko-Fomenko conj ecture, was proved by S. Sadetov [197] in 2004. What can we say about polynomial Poisson brackets of higher degrees?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real (or complex) vector space equipped with a polynomial Poisson bracket $\{\cdot,\cdot\}$, that is, a Poisson bracket on $C^\infty(V)$ (or on the polynomial algebra $\mathbb{R}[V]$) such that the bracket of any two linear coordinate functions is a polynomial on $V$. Recall:

1. A "linear" Poisson bracket on $V$ corresponds to a Lie algebra structure on $V^*$: it is the canonical Lie–Poisson bracket on $\mathfrak{g}^* \cong V$. For such linear brackets, the Mischenko–Fomenko conjecture (proved by Sadetov) asserts that there always exists a complete family of polynomials on $V$ in involution, i.e. a polynomial integrable system.

2. A Poisson pencil is a one-parameter family $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_\lambda = \{\cdot,\cdot\}_1 + \lambda \{\cdot,\cdot\}_2$ of compatible Poisson brackets (any linear combination is again Poisson). A "quadratic + linear" pencil consists of a quadratic Poisson bracket $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_2$ (bracket of linear coordinates is homogeneous of degree $2$) compatible with a linear Poisson bracket $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_1$.

3. A family $\mathcal{F} \subset \mathbb{R}[V]$ of polynomials is said to be in bi-involution with respect to a Poisson pencil if $\{f,g\}_\lambda = 0$ for every $\lambda$ and every $f,g \in \mathcal{F}$. The family is complete (defines an integrable system) if at a generic point $x \in V$, $\dim\, d\mathcal{F}(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}(\dim V + \mathrm{corank}\,\{\cdot,\cdot\}_\lambda$ at $x)$ for generic $\lambda$.

Problem. (a) Investigate concrete examples of "quadratic + linear" Poisson pencils on vector spaces $V$, determine their algebraic types (i.e. the structure of the associated linear pencil of bivectors and the singular set), and for each such pencil construct an explicit complete family of polynomials in bi-involution.

(b) More generally, given a vector space $V$ equipped with a polynomial Poisson bracket of degree $\geq 2$, does there always exist a complete family of Poisson-commuting polynomials on $V$? In other words, does the analogue of the Mischenko–Fomenko theorem hold for polynomial Poisson brackets of higher degree?
artifact.status_search_result: The Mischenko–Fomenko conjecture for linear Poisson brackets was proved by Sadetov (2003/2004). The analogous question for polynomial Poisson brackets of higher degree, and the systematic study of "quadratic + linear" Poisson pencils with construction of complete bi-involutive families, remains an active research direction with only partial results (e.g., families of quadratic Poisson structures on gl(3)* compatible with the Lie–Poisson bracket due to Sokolov and others). No general result establishing existence of complete polynomial integrable systems for arbitrary higher-degree polynomial Poisson brackets has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Poisson brackets with prescribed family of functions in involution
status_evidence.snippet: Quadratic Poisson structures compatible with canonical linear Poisson structures... general theory of such structures and related families of functions in involution.
status_evidence.claim: The study of quadratic+linear Poisson pencils and associated involutive families is an ongoing research area with partial results.

status_evidence.title: Proof of Mishchenko-Fomenko conjecture (1981)
status_evidence.snippet: The Mishchenko–Fomenko conjecture for linear Lie–Poisson brackets was proved by S. T. Sadetov.
status_evidence.claim: The linear case is settled; the higher-degree polynomial case is the natural open extension.
